Corollary 2 Kernel interpolation with the Laplace kernel and adaptive bandwidth is not consistent as n → ∞ in d > 2. Remark 3 The condition γ < 1 could be removed but would require minor additional technicalities. The restriction on s could probably be loosened to s < d. but this condition is of more fundamental nature. While we conjecture that learning with smoother kernels in fixed dimension is not consistent, the proof given in this paper and also the proof from Rakhlin and Zhai (2019) do not extend to s ≥ d. The reason is, loosely speaking, that the RKHS norm of the interpolant is determined by the quantity mini6=j |xi − xj | for s > d while it is governed by the average value −1 P n i minj6=i |xi − xj | for s < d. See also Remark 13 below. 2.3. Proof overview Now we give an overview of the approach used to prove the theorem. As already explained in Rakhlin and Zhai (2019) there are two different failure modes of kernel interpolation as also shown in Figure 1 in their paper. For bandwidths γ > n1/d , i.e., the typical distance between neighbouring points, kernel interpolation will be smooth on scale n−1/d and we will make an error of order (n−1/d )d = n−1 in the ball B(xi , n1/d ) around each data-point. So the total error is bounded from below by a constant. On the other hand, for γ n−1/d , the minimum norm interpolant will be a sum of little hat functions around each data-point and the interpolant will be very small away from the data points. As in Rakhlin and Zhai (2019) we state the result for the different regimes as separate propositions.
